Contact at SubFlow: legal@subflow.com (cc'd on their questionnaire).

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Notice of Subprocessor addition: SubFlow Analytics (Order Form #1379)

Thanks — quick legal triage below. I've attached a redline of our standard MSA flowdown template with the minimum required edits. Attachment: MSA-flowdown-template_redline.docx

Topline: doable, but requires three action items before we can sign-off:

1) Clause flowdown: we must flowsecurity obligations (confidentiality, incident notif, breach cooperation), encryption at-rest/in-transit, logging/retention limits, and subcontractor audit rights. I propose we add an explicit DPA Annex referencing the Order Form and listing SubFlow as a subprocessor; see redline for language.

2) Data residency & scope: If SubFlow will persist raw telemetry in a different region (APAC/EU), we need to either: (a) require data minimization + pseudonymization, or (b) require OrbitWave to route EU traffic to a resident SubFlow instance. Please confirm the geography.

3) Evidence gating: we require SubFlow produce either: (i) current SOC2 report (Type II preferable) or (ii) an independent attestation and a penetration test summary. If SOC2 Type II not available, we'll accept a recent SOC2 Type I + roadmap with mitigations and a three-month monitoring hold.

Logistics notes:
- DocuSign is fine for the DPA annex; procurement should prepare the envelope with a reference to Order Form #1379.
- If OrbitWave insists on an Order Form amendment (versus an annex), we need procurement to track the impact to billing/SLAs.
- The redline flags a section for audit access and escrow — we don't expect escrow in this case but leave the language for future needs.

Please review the redline and call out any vendor-specific asks (e.g., retention windows) to include in the annex. I can push final language once procurement confirms the routing.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com

On the redline: see comments for two optional carveouts (logging retention and telemetry aggregation) — we should try to avoid broad carveouts that weaken incident response.
